We can use reflection to access private methods? Since test class is in same package org.jsoup.parser, we can access package-private members. Private methods need reflection. We'll create test class in same package org.jsoup.parser. We need to construct Token objects. Token is an inner class? Actually Token is a class in Jsoup parser. We'll need to import org.jsoup.parser.Token and its subclasses. Token.StartTag, Token.EndTag, Token.Comment, Token.Character, Token.Doctype. We'll create tokens: new Token.StartTag().name("tag"). etc. The Token class might have builder methods. Token.StartTag has a default constructor; we can set fields via methods. We'll approximate usage. Since we cannot guarantee exact API, we can use reflection to set fields directly. But we can also parse simple XML strings using parseFragment and parse methods to indirectly test functionality. Test insert of XML declaration via comment token: Use insert(Token.Comment) directly by creating a bogus comment token with data "?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?" and bogus true, then verify that a XmlDeclaration node is inserted. However XmlDeclaration class is in org.jsoup.nodes.XmlDeclaration; we can check node type. We need to access insert(Token.Comment) which is package-private; test class in same package can call it. Similarly test popStackToClose: create builder, insert start tags, then call popStackToClose with end tag token, verify stack content. But stack is protected in TreeBuilder? In TreeBuilder, stack is a protected List. So we can access. Use startTag.name("tag"); startTag.selfClosing(boolean) maybe setSelfClosing? In source, there is boolean selfClosing flag accessible via startTag.selfClosing = true; but there is method selfClosing(boolean). We'll try startTag.name("parent"); startTag.selfClosing(false); For attributes: create Attributes attrs = new Attributes(); attrs.put("id", "1"); startTag.attributes(attrs); Similarly for EndTag: Token.EndTag endTag = new Token.EndTag(); endTag.name("parent"); Comment token: Token.Comment comment = new Token.Comment(); comment.data("!xml version='1.0'"); comment.bogus = true; but there may be methods comment.data(String). Use comment.data("!xml version='1.0'"); comment.bogus = true; Might need reflection to set bogus. Character token: Token.Character charToken = new Token.Character(); charToken.data("hello"); Might be method. Doctype token: Token.Doctype doctype = new Token.Doctype(); doctype.name("html"); doctype.publicIdentifier(""); doctype.systemIdentifier(""); doctype.pubSysKey(""); Not sure. Simplify: Use parsing of strings to generate tokens indirectly: Use builder.parseFragment etc. But we need to test insert methods directly. Given complexity, we can rely on parsing strings for most tests and use reflection only for popStackToClose. Thus tests: - testDefaultSettings - testParseSimpleXml - testParseFragment - testXmlDeclarationParsing - testDoctypeParsing - testPopStackToCloseRemovesElements (using reflection to call private method) In testParseSimpleXml we will assert that comment is present and text. Ok. Let's craft code. We'll need to import org.jsoup.Jsoup; org.jsoup.nodes.*; org.jsoup.parser.*; org.jsoup.parser.Token; org.jsoup.parser.ParseErrorList; org.jsoup.parser.ParseSettings; org.jsoup.parser.Parser; org.junit.Test; org.junit.Assert.*; We'll also need java.io.StringReader. Implement testPopStackToCloseRemovesElements: XmlTreeBuilder builder = new XmlTreeBuilder(); // need to initialise internal structures: call builder.initialiseParse(new StringReader(""), "http://example.com", ParseErrorList.noTracking(), ParseSettings.preserveCase); Then create startTag token: Token.StartTag start = new Token.StartTag(); start.name("parent"); start.selfClosing(false); builder.insert(start); // pushes onto stack Now stack size should be 2 (doc + parent). Use reflection to get private method popStackToClose: Method m = XmlTreeBuilder.class.getDeclaredMethod("popStackToClose", Token.EndTag.class); m.setAccessible(true); Token.EndTag end = new Token.EndTag(); end.name("parent"); m.invoke(builder, end); Now after, stack size should be 1 (only doc). Access builder.stack field (protected). Could use reflection to get field 'stack' from TreeBuilder (inherited). Use Field f = TreeBuilder.class.getDeclaredField("stack"); f.setAccessible(true); List stack = (List) f.get(builder); Assert.assertEquals(1, stack.size()); Ok. Now final output with markers.
